comment: Curated public upstream resolvers (issue #877). Every address/hostname pair was checked against the provider's own documentation AND probed live with `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:853 -verify_hostname <name> -verify_return_error`, which is exactly what BIND9's strict remote-hostname does. IPv6 rows are documentation-verified only. Re-verify before editing: with DoT verification on, a stale hostname does not degrade to plaintext, it fails closed and the group SERVFAILs every query.

presets.name: Cloudflare
presets.description: Anycast resolver with no content filtering.
presets.notes: The certificate also carries one.one.one.one, so either name validates.

presets.name: Cloudflare Security
presets.description: Blocks known malware and phishing domains.
presets.notes: Blocked names answer 0.0.0.0 rather than NXDOMAIN.

presets.name: Cloudflare Family
presets.description: Blocks malware, phishing and adult content.
presets.notes: Blocked names answer 0.0.0.0 rather than NXDOMAIN.

presets.name: Google Public DNS
presets.description: Large anycast resolver, no content filtering.
presets.notes: Not unconditionally open: Google honours court-ordered blocks in several jurisdictions (BE, FR, IN, IT, PT) and answers REFUSED for those names.

presets.name: Quad9
presets.description: Blocks malicious domains using threat intelligence; DNSSEC validating.
presets.notes: Answers NXDOMAIN for blocked names, so it does not collide with downstream DNSSEC validation the way forged-address filtering does.

presets.name: Quad9 (no blocklist)
presets.description: Quad9 without the malware blocklist. Still DNSSEC validating.
presets.notes: Widely still described as 'unsecured / no DNSSEC'. That is out of date: Quad9 enabled DNSSEC validation on every endpoint on 2026-06-15, so this address validates too. It differs from 9.9.9.9 only by dropping the malware blocklist.

presets.name: Quad9 (ECS)
presets.description: Quad9 with EDNS Client Subnet, for CDN-sensitive deployments.
presets.notes: Sends client subnet upstream, which improves CDN locality at the cost of leaking a prefix of the client address.

presets.name: OpenDNS
presets.notes: Cisco does not publish a DoT hostname; this name is taken from the live certificate (CN doh.opendns.com, SANs include dns.opendns.com) and verified against both addresses.

presets.name: OpenDNS FamilyShield
presets.description: Blocks adult content, proxies and phishing.
presets.notes: IPv4 only on purpose. Cisco's IPv6 addresses are not documented as FamilyShield resolvers and are reported not to apply the family filter, so shipping them here would advertise protection that silently does not apply.

presets.name: AdGuard Family Protection
presets.description: Blocks ads, trackers and adult content; forces Safe Search.
presets.notes: Also rewrites search engines to their Safe Search endpoints.

presets.name: AdGuard (unfiltered)
presets.description: AdGuard infrastructure with no filtering applied.

presets.name: Mullvad (base)
presets.description: Privacy-focused resolver blocking ads, trackers and malware.
presets.notes: Encrypted transport only — Mullvad answers REFUSED on plaintext port 53, so selecting this without DoT breaks every query. One address per variant; there is no secondary.

presets.name: Mullvad (adblock)
presets.description: Mullvad resolver blocking ads and trackers only.
presets.notes: Encrypted transport only — Mullvad answers REFUSED on plaintext port 53. One address per variant; there is no secondary.

presets.name: DNS4EU (protective)
presets.description: EU-operated resolver blocking malicious and fraudulent domains.
presets.notes: DNS4EU documents a single address per variant, so only that one ships here; add a secondary by hand if the provider publishes one.

presets.name: DNS4EU (unfiltered)
presets.notes: DNS4EU documents a single address per variant, so only that one ships here.
